title: Zero Trust Doesn't Fully Solve the Agentic AI Problem
partialText: Zero Trust security was designed around identities accessing resources. Agentic AI introduces a different challenge: autonomous systems that reason, plan, and execute actions with real-world consequences. This article explores emerging risks including prompt injection, tool misuse, privilege chaining, and auditability gaps, and proposes an agentic security framework built around action authorization, behavioral baselines, reasoning transparency, and human checkpoints.

title: Let AI Models Fight Over Your Architecture
partialText: Asking a single AI to design your system is a mistake. Single prompts yield generic, happy-path answers. Instead, developers should build multi-agent workflows where specialized AIs—like an Architect, Red-Team, and Evaluator, actively debate the architecture. By forcing LLMs to propose, critique, and score tradeoffs against simpler baselines, you avoid brittle chatbot responses. The result is an automated architecture review board that outputs production-ready Decision Records.

title: Suffering From Marketing Paralysis? Everyone Is Right Now, Here’s The Way Out
partialText: Open-ended AI development cycles open competitive space as marketers contend with the lack of traditional SaaS launch sequences and evolving go to market strategy. A cohort-based process aligns with AI development and sales, with dynamic, customer-informed narratives.

title: Building a Read-Only AI Agent for Storage Incident Response
partialText: Agentic AI can be useful in cloud storage operations, but its first production role should be read-only investigation rather than auto-remediation. This article argues for giving AI agents access to metrics, logs, traces, deployments, tickets, and topology so they can produce structured incident briefs with timelines, blast radius, ranked hypotheses, confidence scores, and auditable evidence while leaving production changes to human engineers.

title: Hands-Off Coding on GCP: Building Autonomous Agents with Guardrails
partialText: This article outlines an architecture for autonomous background coding agents built on Google Cloud Platform. Rather than focusing on prompting alone, it frames AI coding as an orchestration and infrastructure problem involving isolated runtimes, deterministic workflows, secure execution environments, task queues, observability, and pull-request automation. Using services like Cloud Run Jobs, Vertex AI, Cloud Workflows, Firestore, and Secret Manager, the piece argues that reliable AI software development depends more on process discipline and governance than raw model capability.

title: How I Built a Pipeline to Restore Old B&W Photos to 4K Color Using Open-Source AI
partialText: I tested 8 different open-source AI upscalers and restoration tools to find the best pipeline for converting old black-and-white film footage into 4K colorized images for a YouTube history channel. After days of testing on rented GPU servers, the winning pipeline is surprisingly simple: Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 does everything — upscale, restore, AND colorize — in a single prompt, in under 60 seconds.

title: Every Tool You Give an AI Agent Becomes a Security Decision
partialText: As AI agents gain access to tools and real-world systems, traditional chatbot security models become insufficient. This article argues that sensitive actions should never rely solely on model output. Instead, authorization, validation, policy enforcement, audit logging, and business-rule checks should sit outside the model and as close as possible to the tool being invoked. The goal is simple: the agent requests, deterministic controls decide, and the tool executes only if allowed.

title: 6 Failure Modes I Test Every AI Startup Idea Against Before Writing Code
partialText: Most AI models will validate almost any startup idea. This article proposes a different approach: use AI to argue why the idea will fail.
